newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says joins Caspian Azeri oil group.
newsitem.headline: Iran says joins Caspian Azeri oil group.

text.p: Iran's Oil Industries Engineering Company has signed a deal in Baku acquiring 10 percent of an international oil consortium that will tap crude oil in Azerbaijan's sector of the Caspian Sea, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Wednesday.
It said in a Baku-datelined article the deal was signed on Tuesday for the development of Len-Koran and Talysh-Deniz fields.

"A contract was signed here Tuesday for the membership of the private Oil Industries Engineering Company (OIEC) of Iran in the consortium...According to the agreement, the state oil company of the Azerbaijan republic SOCAR will give 10 percent of the developing shares in the said oil fields to OIEC," it said.

It quoted the managing director of OIEC, Ali Akbar Hashemi, as saying the agreement paved the way for the expansion of the company's activities in Azerbaijan. "According to Hashemi, all the members of the consortium have welcomed the participation of OIEC in the contract," it added.
IRNA put the cost of the project at $1.5-$2 billion.

Germany's Veba AG unit Deminex on Tuesday joined the consortium with a 10 percent stake. The consortium also includes France's Elf Aquitaine with 40 percent, Total with 10 percent, Agip of Italy and Petrofina of Belgium, each with five percent. SOCAR also has a stake.
The 30-year project south of the Azeri capital involves fields containing up to 140 million tonnes of recoverable oil. Peak output would probably reach 25 million tonnes a year.
